How this was found

a climb is circling flight of at least 60 s with at least 80 m height gain, counted only after the engine stopped (detected with the logger's noise sensor). Climbs within 2.5 km of each other were grouped together, and a group counts as a hotspot when 5 or more different flights and at least 3 different pilots used it, so one pilot's habits don't create a hotspot. The heatmap divides, for each 1 km square, the number of flights that climbed near it by the number that flew near it, smoothed and compared with the average for the whole area (about 7%). D-KJPL (two pilots) counts as one pilot. Heights are GPS altitude MSL; Veronica is about 1,345 m. Times are local (UTC+2). With this many flights it's a pattern, not proof. Thermals drift downwind and depend on the day. Roads, towns and airfields come from the XCSoar Namibia map; airspace from your OpenSoar airspace file. Not for navigation.
